# Finding animation for brick and window interaction (2026-02-03 12:55Z)

_**User (2026-02-03 13:46Z)**_

ok lets recap, we want to find an animation that plays when using object 4 (brick) with hotspot 294 (window).

When this happens a series of actions are executed:
 - A special alfred animation plays (this is what we are trying to find!). Based on observation, this animation is around 71 pixels wide and 3 frames total.
 - The brick sprite from room 3 (sprite 7 in the room metadata) is displayed and probably moved manually (hardcoded) towards the window, which is near the top of the screen.
 - A "sticker" is placed on the window. This sticker is at offset 34089 in alfred.6
 - A sound is played. this is sound in slot 2 in the room, "GLASS1ZZ.SMP"
 - A conversation happens by reading texts in JUEGO.EXE (three consecutive texts starting in 0x000443A0 in the file, then 0x000443BF, then 0x000443DD, offsets might be wrong by 1 byte).
 - Alfred leaves the room through the right exit; it looks like the game does this by simulating a click on the right edge of the screen

 Remember we are trying to find the animation of alfred throwing the brick (the first item on the list). Use ghidra for this, if everything else fails we can try debugging with dosbox but the current instructions on the project arent valid.

```json
{
```

```json
  "commandLine": {
    "original": "python3 -c \"\nimport struct\n\nwith open('files/JUEGO.EXE', 'rb') as f:\n    data = f.read()\n\n# The table is at memory 0x48118\n# Let me find the file-to-memory mapping by looking for known patterns\n\n# From Ghidra: str_alfred_1_filename at 0x401AF = 'alfred.1'\n# Let's search for 'alfred.1' in the file\nalfred1 = b'alfred.1\\\\x00'\nfor i in range(len(data) - 10):\n    if data[i:i+len(alfred1)] == alfred1:\n        print(f'Found alfred.1 at file offset 0x{i:05X}')\n        # Memory offset 0x401AF\n        # file_offset = i, mem_offset = 0x401AF\n        # offset = file - mem\n        offset_diff = i - 0x401AF\n        print(f'File = Memory + 0x{offset_diff:05X}')\n        print()\n        \n        # Now find the combo table at memory 0x48118\n        combo_table_file = 0x48118 + offset_diff\n        print(f'Combo table (0x48118) at file 0x{combo_table_file:05X}')\n        \n        # Read entries\n        print()\n        print('Combo table entries:')\n        for j in range(100):\n            off = combo_table_file + j * 8\n            if off + 8 &gt; len(data):\n                break\n            item1, item2, handler = struct.unpack('&lt;HHI', data[off:off+8])\n            if item1 == 0xFFFF:\n                print(f'[{j:2d}] TERMINATOR')\n                break\n            if (item1 == 294 and item2 == 4) or (item1 == 4 and item2 == 294):\n                print(f'[{j:2d}] item1={item1:4d}, item2={item2:3d}, handler=0x{handler:08X}  **BRICK+WINDOW**')\n            elif item1 == 4 or item2 == 4:\n                print(f'[{j:2d}] item1={item1:4d}, item2={item2:3d}, handler=0x{handler:08X}  (brick)')\n            elif item1 == 294 or item2 == 294:\n                print(f'[{j:2d}] item1={item1:4d}, item2={item2:3d}, handler=0x{handler:08X}  (window)')\n        break\n\" 2&gt;&amp;1",
```

```json
  "textEditContent": "#!/usr/bin/env python3\n\"\"\"Find the brick+window combo handler by mapping file to memory addresses.\"\"\"\n\nimport struct\n\nwith open(\"files/JUEGO.EXE\", \"rb\") as f:\n    data = f.read()\n\n# The table is at memory 0x48118\n# Let me find the file-to-memory mapping by looking for known patterns\n\n# From Ghidra: str_alfred_1_filename at 0x401AF = 'alfred.1'\n# Let's search for 'alfred.1' in the file\nalfred1 = b'alfred.1\\x00'\nfor i in range(len(data) - 10):\n    if data[i:i+len(alfred1)] == alfred1:\n        print(f\"Found 'alfred.1' at file offset 0x{i:05X}\")\n        # Memory offset 0x401AF\n        # file_offset = i, mem_offset = 0x401AF\n        # offset = file - mem\n        offset_diff = i - 0x401AF\n        print(f\"File = Memory + 0x{offset_diff:05X}\")\n        print()\n        \n        # Now find the combo table at memory 0x48118\n        combo_table_file = 0x48118 + offset_diff\n        print(f\"Combo table (0x48118) at file 0x{combo_table_file:05X}\")\n        \n        # Read entries\n        print()\n        print(\"Combo table entries:\")\n        print(\"-\" * 70)\n        for j in range(100):\n            off = combo_table_file + j * 8\n            if off + 8 &gt; len(data):\n                break\n            item1, item2, handler = struct.unpack(\"&lt;HHI\", data[off:off+8])\n            if item1 == 0xFFFF:\n                print(f\"[{j:2d}] TERMINATOR\")\n                break\n            note = \"\"\n            if (item1 == 294 and item2 == 4) or (item1 == 4 and item2 == 294):\n                note = \" **BRICK+WINDOW**\"\n            elif item1 == 4 or item2 == 4:\n                note = \" (brick)\"\n            elif item1 == 294 or item2 == 294:\n                note = \" (window)\"\n            print(f\"[{j:2d}] item1={item1:4d}, item2={item2:3d}, handler=0x{handler:08X}{note}\")\n        break\n",
  "toolCallResult": null
}
```

```json
    "original": "python3 -c \"\nimport struct\n# The handler 0x1284B is at file offset 0x1284B + 0x4200 = 0x16A4B\n# (Adding 0x4200 for CODE section offset)\n# Wait - check file mapping more carefully\n\n# In DOS LE format, code starts after headers\n# From previous analysis, the mapping should be:\n# Memory address - file offset difference\n\n# Let's just read around the combo table file offset to see the data\nwith open('/Users/gabriel/Desktop/source/alfredtools/files/JUEGO.EXE', 'rb') as f:\n    # The brick+window handler is 0x1284B\n    # File offset for code = memory - 0x4200 (our DATA offset was 0x3200)\n    # But let's verify by reading the actual bytes and comparing\n    \n    # Find where 0x1284B points in the file\n    # The combo table is at file 0x4B318 = memory 0x48118\n    # So DATA offset is 0x4B318 - 0x48118 = 0x3200\n    \n    # But handlers are code addresses, not data\n    # Let's check what the execute_complex_item_script_table does\n    # It reads the handler and calls it: CALL [handler]\n    \n    # Handler 0x1284B is a direct code address in flat memory\n    # For CODE sections, the file offset might be different\n    \n    # show_action_menu_popup is at 0x124AD\n    # Let's find where it is in the file by searching for known bytes\n    f.seek(0)\n    data = f.read()\n    \n    # Search for the PUSH 0x01 pattern that starts show_action_menu_popup\n    # Actually, let's search for a unique byte sequence near 0x1284B\n    \n    # The function list shows:\n    # show_action_menu_popup @ 0x124AD\n    # main_menu_handler @ 0x12918\n    # Handler 0x1284B should be in between\n    \n    # Try different file offsets\n    for base in [0x4200, 0x3200, 0x0]:\n        file_offset = 0x1284B + base\n        if file_offset &lt; len(data):\n            f.seek(file_offset)\n            sample = f.read(16)\n            print(f'Offset 0x1284B + 0x{base:X} = 0x{file_offset:X}: {sample.hex()}')\n\"\n",
```

```json
  "textEditContent": "#!/usr/bin/env python3\"\"\"Analyze the brick+window combo handler at 0x1284B\"\"\"import structJUEGO_PATH = \"files/JUEGO.EXE\"with open(JUEGO_PATH, \"rb\") as f:    data = f.read()# The brick+window handler is at memory address 0x1284B# Based on previous analysis, code section file offset = memory + 0x4200# But let me verify with a known function# show_action_menu_popup is at memory 0x124AD# Let's find its signature in the file# From Ghidra disassembly of show_action_menu_popup, first instructions are:# 000124ad: PUSH EBX# The opcode for PUSH EBX is 0x53# Search for the byte pattern we know starts main_menu_handler at 0x12918# 00012918: PUSH 0x54 = 0x6A 0x54search_patterns = [    (0x12918, bytes([0x6A, 0x54]), \"main_menu_handler PUSH 0x54\"),]for mem_addr, pattern, name in search_patterns:    # Try different base offsets    for base in [0x4200, 0x3200, 0x0, -0x1000, 0x1000]:        file_off = mem_addr + base        if 0 &lt;= file_off &lt; len(data) - len(pattern):            if data[file_off:file_off+len(pattern)] == pattern:                print(f\"FOUND: {name} at file 0x{file_off:X} (base offset 0x{base:X})\")                print(f\"  Memory 0x{mem_addr:X} = File 0x{file_off:X}\")                print(f\"  File = Memory + 0x{base:X}\")# Actually, let me look for the pattern anywhere in the fileprint(\"\\nSearching for PUSH 0x54 (0x6A 0x54) in file...\")for i in range(len(data) - 2):    if data[i:i+2] == bytes([0x6A, 0x54]):        # Check if next instruction looks like CALL        if data[i+2] == 0xE8:  # CALL rel32            print(f\"  Found at file 0x{i:X}\")# Now let's look at the actual combo table call mechanismprint(\"\\n\" + \"=\"*60)print(\"Looking at how execute_complex_item_script_table calls handlers\")print(\"=\"*60)# The decompiled code shows:# (*(code *)(&amp;PTR_LAB_0004811c)[(extraout_EDX &amp; 0xff) * 2])();# This means it reads a pointer from address 0x4811c + index*8 and calls it# 0x4811c = 0x48118 + 4 (skipping item1 and item2 fields)# So the handler field at offset +4 in each entry is a direct code pointer# Let me check what the file looks like around where 0x1284B would be# if code_file_offset = code_mem + something# Known: combo table at file 0x4B318, memory 0x48118# Diff = 0x4B318 - 0x48118 = 0x3200 (this is for DATA)# For CODE, let's find a known code sequence# The combo table points to function at 0x127B2 for the first entry# Let's see what's thereprint(\"\\nCombo table entries (from file):\")f_offset = 0x4B318  # combo table file offsetfor i in range(5):    entry_off = f_offset + i * 8    item1, item2, handler = struct.unpack('&lt;HHI', data[entry_off:entry_off+8])    print(f\"Entry {i}: item1={item1}, item2={item2}, handler=0x{handler:05X}\")        # Try to find what code might be at this handler    # CODE section difference: let's assume it's the same 0x3200    # Actually for DOS LE, code and data might have same base    code_file_off = handler + 0x3200    if 0 &lt;= code_file_off &lt; len(data):        sample = data[code_file_off:code_file_off+10]        print(f\"  File 0x{code_file_off:05X}: {sample.hex()}\")print(\"\\n\" + \"=\"*60)print(\"Searching for brick+window handler code at 0x1284B\")print(\"=\"*60)# The handler 0x1284B should be a function that:# 1. Plays an animation for Alfred throwing the brick# 2. Moves the brick sprite toward the window# 3. Places a sticker on the window# 4. Plays GLASS1ZZ.SMP sound# 5. Shows conversation text# 6. Alfred leaves through right exit# Try various offsets to find where 0x1284B maps tohandler_addr = 0x1284Bfor offset in [0x3200, 0x4200, 0x3000, 0x3100, 0x3300]:    file_pos = handler_addr + offset    if file_pos &lt; len(data):        sample = data[file_pos:file_pos+32]        print(f\"0x1284B + 0x{offset:04X} = file 0x{file_pos:05X}: {sample.hex()}\")\n",
  "toolCallResult": null
```

```json
{
```
```json
  "invocationMessage": "Creating [](file:///Users/gabriel/Desktop/source/alfredtools/analyze_combo_handler.py)",
```

```json
  "content": "",
  "textEditContent": "#!/usr/bin/env python3\n\"\"\"\nAnalyze the brick+window combo handler address.\n\"\"\"\n\nimport struct\n\ndef mem_to_file(mem_addr):\n    \"\"\"Convert memory address to file offset for CODE section.\"\"\"\n    return mem_addr + 0x4200\n\ndef main():\n    with open('files/JUEGO.EXE', 'rb') as f:\n        # The combo table entry for brick+window is at memory 0x48118 + 8 = 0x48120\n        # But let's look at the handler address: 0x1284B\n        \n        handler_addr = 0x1284B\n        file_off = mem_to_file(handler_addr)\n        \n        print(f\"Handler address: 0x{handler_addr:06X}\")\n        print(f\"File offset: 0x{file_off:06X}\")\n        print()\n        \n        # Read 256 bytes starting from the handler\n        f.seek(file_off)\n        code = f.read(0x100)\n        \n        print(\"Raw bytes from handler address:\")\n        for i in range(0, 80, 16):\n            addr = handler_addr + i\n            chunk = code[i:i+16]\n            hex_str = ' '.join(f'{b:02X}' for b in chunk)\n            print(f\"  0x{addr:06X}: {hex_str}\")\n        \n        print()\n        print(\"Analysis:\")\n        print(\"  First bytes: 1D 9E FB 00 00\")\n        print(\"  This is: SBB EAX, 0x0000FB9E (subtract with borrow)\")\n        print(\"  Which is unusual for a function entry point.\")\n        print()\n        \n        # Let's look at what Ghidra sees at 0x12849 (2 bytes before)\n        f.seek(mem_to_file(0x12843))\n        context = f.read(20)\n        print(\"Context from 0x12843:\")\n        hex_str = ' '.join(f'{b:02X}' for b in context)\n        print(f\"  {hex_str}\")\n        print()\n        \n        # The issue is that the combo table entry might use a different\n        # segment/offset calculation. Let's verify the table itself.\n        \n        print(\"Checking combo table entry directly:\")\n        # Table at 0x48118, entry 1 starts at +8\n        # File offset: 0x48118 - 0x10000 + 0x14200 = 0x4B318\n        table_off = 0x4B318 + 8  # Entry 1\n        f.seek(table_off)\n        entry = f.read(8)\n        item1, item2, handler = struct.unpack('&lt;HHI', entry)\n        print(f\"  Entry bytes: {entry.hex()}\")\n        print(f\"  item1={item1} (0x{item1:04X})\")\n        print(f\"  item2={item2} (0x{item2:04X})\")\n        print(f\"  handler=0x{handler:08X}\")\n\nif __name__ == '__main__':\n    main()\n",
  "toolCallResult": null
}
```

```json
  "textEditContent": "#!/usr/bin/env python3\n\"\"\"\nSearch ALFRED.7 for potential brick throw animations.\nLooking for: ~71 pixels wide, ~3 frames, likely near FIGHT animation.\n\nThe animation format appears to be:\n- BUDA marker (4 bytes) appears at start\n- Then raw pixel data (width * height * frames bytes)\n- Or RLE compressed\n\nKnown animations from offsets.h:\n- READ_BOOK: 559685, 10 frames, 51x102\n- READ_RECIPE: 578943, 10 frames, 51x102\n- ELECTRIC_SHOCK_1: 37000, 3 frames, 45x87\n- ELECTRIC_SHOCK_3: 53106, 2 frames, 82x58\n- FIGHT: 0x2207FA (2230266), 11 frames, 71x102\n\"\"\"\n\nimport struct\n\nALFRED7_PATH = \"files/ALFRED.7\"\n\ndef find_buda_markers(data):\n    \"\"\"Find all BUDA marker positions.\"\"\"\n    markers = []\n    for i in range(len(data) - 4):\n        if data[i:i+4] == b'BUDA':\n            markers.append(i)\n    return markers\n\ndef main():\n    with open(ALFRED7_PATH, 'rb') as f:\n        data = f.read()\n    \n    print(f\"ALFRED.7 size: {len(data)} bytes (0x{len(data):X})\")\n    print()\n    \n    buda_positions = find_buda_markers(data)\n    print(f\"Found {len(buda_positions)} BUDA markers\")\n    print()\n    \n    # Known animation offsets (where BUDA markers should be near)\n    known = {\n        559685: (\"READ_BOOK\", 10, 51, 102),\n        578943: (\"READ_RECIPE\", 10, 51, 102),\n        37000: (\"ELECTRIC_SHOCK_1\", 3, 45, 87),\n        53106: (\"ELECTRIC_SHOCK_3\", 2, 82, 58),\n        2230266: (\"FIGHT\", 11, 71, 102),\n    }\n    \n    # Find which BUDA markers are used vs unused\n    used_budas = set()\n    \n    for offset, (name, frames, w, h) in known.items():\n        # Check for BUDA at offset-4\n        if offset - 4 in buda_positions:\n            print(f\"{name}: BUDA at {offset-4} (0x{offset-4:X})\")\n            used_budas.add(offset - 4)\n        elif offset in buda_positions:\n            print(f\"{name}: BUDA at {offset} (0x{offset:X})\")\n            used_budas.add(offset)\n        else:\n            # Find nearest BUDA\n            nearest = min(buda_positions, key=lambda x: abs(x - offset))\n            print(f\"{name}: Nearest BUDA at {nearest} (0x{nearest:X}), delta={nearest-offset}\")\n    \n    print()\n    print(\"=\"*60)\n    print(\"Looking for unidentified animations near FIGHT (0x2207FA)...\")\n    print(\"=\"*60)\n    \n    # FIGHT is at 0x2207FA with BUDA at 0x2207F6\n    fight_offset = 0x2207FA\n    fight_buda = 0x2207F6\n    fight_size = 71 * 102 * 11  # Total pixel data\n    \n    # Look for BUDA markers BEFORE the fight animation\n    # These would be other Alfred special animations\n    \n    before_fight = [p for p in buda_positions if p &lt; fight_buda and p &gt; fight_buda - 100000]\n    print(f\"BUDA markers in 100KB before FIGHT: {len(before_fight)}\")\n    \n    for pos in sorted(before_fight, reverse=True)[:20]:\n        # Check if this could be a 3-frame animation around 71 pixels wide\n        # Data starts at pos+4\n        frame_data_start = pos + 4\n        \n        # Try different dimension combinations\n        candidates = []\n        for w in range(60, 80):\n            for h in range(80, 120):\n                for frames in [2, 3, 4, 5]:\n                    size = w * h * frames\n                    # Check if there's another BUDA marker at expected end\n                    expected_end = frame_data_start + size\n                    if expected_end in buda_positions or abs(expected_end - pos) &lt; 100:\n                        candidates.append((w, h, frames, size))\n        \n        # Read some bytes after BUDA\n        sample = data[frame_data_start:frame_data_start+16]\n        print(f\"  BUDA at 0x{pos:06X}: {sample.hex()[:32]}...\")\n    \n    print()\n    print(\"=\"*60)\n    print(\"Checking specific potential throw animation areas...\")\n    print(\"=\"*60)\n    \n    # The throw animation should be relatively small: 3 frames * ~71 * ~100 = ~21,300 bytes\n    # Let's look for BUDA markers followed by ~21KB of data before next BUDA\n    \n    for i, pos in enumerate(buda_positions):\n        if i + 1 &lt; len(buda_positions):\n            next_pos = buda_positions[i + 1]\n            gap = next_pos - pos - 4  # Data between this BUDA and next\n            \n            # Look for gaps around 20-25KB (3 frames of ~70x100)\n            if 18000 &lt; gap &lt; 25000:\n                # Check if dimensions work out\n                for frames in [3, 4]:\n                    for w in range(65, 80):\n                        h = gap // (w * frames)\n                        if 80 &lt;= h &lt;= 110 and w * h * frames == gap:\n                            print(f\"Potential animation at 0x{pos:06X}: {w}x{h} x {frames} frames = {gap} bytes\")\n                            # Read first few bytes\n                            sample = data[pos+4:pos+20]\n                            print(f\"  Data: {sample.hex()}\")\n\nif __name__ == '__main__':\n    main()\n",
```

```json
  "isConfirmed": {
```

```json
  "content": "",
  "textEditContent": "#!/usr/bin/env python3\n\"\"\"\nSearch for raw (uncompressed) animations in ALFRED.7.\nThe brick throw would be uncompressed like ELECTRIC_SHOCK animations.\n\nLooking for: ~71 wide, ~100 tall, 3 frames = ~21,300 bytes of sequential pixel data\n\"\"\"\n\nimport struct\nfrom collections import defaultdict\n\nALFRED7_PATH = \"files/ALFRED.7\"\n\ndef find_buda_markers(data):\n    \"\"\"Find all BUDA marker positions.\"\"\"\n    markers = []\n    for i in range(len(data) - 4):\n        if data[i:i+4] == b'BUDA':\n            markers.append(i)\n    return markers\n\ndef analyze_raw_data(data, offset, length):\n    \"\"\"Analyze a chunk of data for animation characteristics.\"\"\"\n    chunk = data[offset:offset+length]\n    \n    # Count unique values\n    hist = defaultdict(int)\n    for b in chunk:\n        hist[b] += 1\n    \n    # Check for transparency marker (0xFF often)\n    ff_count = hist.get(0xFF, 0)\n    zero_count = hist.get(0x00, 0)\n    \n    return {\n        'unique_values': len(hist),\n        'ff_ratio': ff_count / length if length &gt; 0 else 0,\n        'zero_ratio': zero_count / length if length &gt; 0 else 0,\n        'sample': chunk[:20].hex() if len(chunk) &gt;= 20 else chunk.hex()\n    }\n\ndef main():\n    with open(ALFRED7_PATH, 'rb') as f:\n        data = f.read()\n    \n    print(f\"ALFRED.7 size: {len(data)} bytes\")\n    print()\n    \n    buda_positions = find_buda_markers(data)\n    print(f\"Found {len(buda_positions)} BUDA markers\")\n    \n    # Known uncompressed animations (numBudas = 0)\n    # ELECTRIC_SHOCK_1: 37000, 3 frames, 45x87 = 11745 bytes\n    # ELECTRIC_SHOCK_3: 53106, 2 frames, 82x58 = 9512 bytes\n    \n    print()\n    print(\"=\"*60)\n    print(\"Analyzing known uncompressed animations...\")\n    print(\"=\"*60)\n    \n    elec1 = 37000\n    elec1_size = 3 * 45 * 87\n    info = analyze_raw_data(data, elec1, elec1_size)\n    print(f\"ELECTRIC_SHOCK_1 at {elec1}: {info}\")\n    \n    elec3 = 53106\n    elec3_size = 2 * 82 * 58  \n    info = analyze_raw_data(data, elec3, elec3_size)\n    print(f\"ELECTRIC_SHOCK_3 at {elec3}: {info}\")\n    \n    # Check FIGHT animation (also uncompressed based on code)\n    fight = 0x2207FA\n    fight_size = 11 * 71 * 102\n    info = analyze_raw_data(data, fight, fight_size)\n    print(f\"FIGHT at 0x{fight:X}: {info}\")\n    \n    print()\n    print(\"=\"*60)\n    print(\"Searching for potential throw animation (raw/uncompressed)...\")\n    print(\"=\"*60)\n    \n    # The throw animation should be:\n    # - Around 71 pixels wide (like FIGHT)\n    # - Around 100 pixels tall (like FIGHT)\n    # - 3 frames\n    # - NOT preceded by BUDA marker (uncompressed)\n    # - Have a lot of 0xFF (transparency) at edges\n    \n    # Search in areas NOT near BUDA markers\n    target_size = 71 * 100 * 3  # ~21,300 bytes\n    \n    # Check every 1000 bytes for potential animation start\n    candidates = []\n    \n    for offset in range(0, len(data) - target_size, 1000):\n        # Skip if near a BUDA marker\n        near_buda = any(abs(offset - b) &lt; 500 for b in buda_positions)\n        if near_buda:\n            continue\n        \n        info = analyze_raw_data(data, offset, target_size)\n        \n        # Good candidate if:\n        # - High FF ratio (transparency around Alfred)\n        # - Many unique values (actual pixel art, not repeated patterns)\n        if info['ff_ratio'] &gt; 0.3 and info['unique_values'] &gt; 50:\n            candidates.append((offset, info))\n    \n    print(f\"Found {len(candidates)} potential candidates\")\n    for offset, info in candidates[:10]:\n        print(f\"  0x{offset:06X}: {info}\")\n    \n    # Also check near known animations\n    print()\n    print(\"=\"*60)\n    print(\"Checking near ELECTRIC_SHOCK animations...\")\n    print(\"=\"*60)\n    \n    # ELECTRIC_SHOCK_1 is at 37000, might have other animations nearby\n    for delta in [-30000, -20000, -10000, 10000, 20000, 30000]:\n        check = elec1 + delta\n        if 0 &lt; check &lt; len(data) - target_size:\n            info = analyze_raw_data(data, check, target_size)\n            near = any(abs(check - b) &lt; 100 for b in buda_positions)\n            print(f\"  0x{check:06X}: ff={info['ff_ratio']:.2f}, unique={info['unique_values']}, near_buda={near}\")\n\nif __name__ == '__main__':\n    main()\n",
  "toolCallResult": null
}
```

```json
    "original": "python3 -c \"\nwith open('files/ALFRED.7', 'rb') as f:\n    # Check FIGHT animation area\n    fight = 0x2207FA\n    \n    # Check for BUDA marker before\n    f.seek(fight - 8)\n    pre = f.read(16)\n    print(f'Bytes around FIGHT (0x{fight:X}):')\n    print(f'  -8 to +8: {pre.hex()}')\n    \n    # BUDA should be at fight - 4\n    f.seek(fight - 4)\n    buda = f.read(4)\n    print(f'  BUDA check at -4: {buda}')\n    \n    # Read actual data\n    f.seek(fight)\n    data = f.read(32)\n    print(f'  Data at offset: {data.hex()}')\n    \n    # The data 68ff050041ff0100... looks like RLE\n    # Let me decode: 68 FF 05 00 = run of 0x68 (104) FF bytes, then 05 00 = 5 bytes of something\n    # Wait, that doesn't match the RLE format I know\n\" 2&gt;&amp;1",
```

```json
    "original": "python3 -c \"\nwith open('files/ALFRED.7', 'rb') as f:\n    # Check the candidate at 0x1AF3EA\n    offset = 0x1AF3EA\n    \n    f.seek(offset - 10)\n    context = f.read(40)\n    print(f'Context around 0x{offset:06X}:')\n    print(f'  {context.hex()}')\n    \n    # Check for BUDA\n    if b'BUDA' in context:\n        print('  Contains BUDA marker!')\n        buda_pos = context.find(b'BUDA')\n        print(f'  BUDA at offset-10+{buda_pos} = 0x{offset-10+buda_pos:06X}')\n    \n    # Read data at exact offset\n    f.seek(offset)\n    data = f.read(100)\n    print(f'\\\\nData at 0x{offset:06X}:')\n    print(f'  {data[:32].hex()}')\n    \n    # Analyze characteristics\n    from collections import Counter\n    # Read ~21KB for analysis\n    f.seek(offset)\n    anim_data = f.read(71 * 100 * 3)  # Approximate size\n    counter = Counter(anim_data)\n    ff_count = counter.get(0xFF, 0)\n    total = len(anim_data)\n    print(f'\\\\nCharacteristics ({total} bytes):')\n    print(f'  0xFF ratio: {ff_count/total:.2%}')\n    print(f'  Unique values: {len(counter)}')\n\" 2&gt;&amp;1",
```

```json
  "textEditContent": "#!/usr/bin/env python3\n\"\"\"\nTry to decode the potential brick throw animation at 0x1AF3E6 (BUDA).\nUses the RLE decompression similar to ScummVM's mergeRleBlocks.\n\"\"\"\n\nimport struct\nfrom PIL import Image\nimport os\n\nALFRED7_PATH = \"files/ALFRED.7\"\n\ndef read_until_buda(data, start):\n    \"\"\"Read data until BUDA marker or end.\"\"\"\n    end = start\n    while end &lt; len(data) - 3:\n        if data[end:end+4] == b'BUDA':\n            break\n        end += 1\n    return data[start:end]\n\ndef rle_decompress(data, max_output=640*400):\n    \"\"\"\n    Decompress RLE data. Format:\n    - High nibble indicates run type\n    - If byte &gt;= 0x80: run length encoded (repeat next byte N times)\n    - Otherwise: literal bytes\n    \n    Actually the format seems to be:\n    XXFF YYZZ where XX is length of something, FF is marker, etc.\n    \n    Let me try another interpretation based on the FIGHT data pattern:\n    68ff050041ff0100050c01003dff0400040c0500\n    \n    This looks like: length_low, FF, length_high, ...\n    \"\"\"\n    output = []\n    i = 0\n    \n    # First, let's just try treating it as raw data to see what we get\n    return data[:max_output]\n\ndef extract_animation(data, buda_offset, width, height, num_frames):\n    \"\"\"Extract animation from BUDA-marked data.\"\"\"\n    # Data starts after BUDA (4 bytes)\n    data_start = buda_offset + 4\n    \n    # Find next BUDA to determine size\n    end = data_start\n    while end &lt; len(data) - 3:\n        if data[end:end+4] == b'BUDA':\n            break\n        end += 1\n    \n    compressed_size = end - data_start\n    print(f\"Compressed data: {compressed_size} bytes (0x{data_start:06X} to 0x{end:06X})\")\n    \n    # Expected raw size for animation\n    raw_size = width * height * num_frames\n    print(f\"Expected raw size: {raw_size} bytes ({width}x{height}x{num_frames})\")\n    \n    compressed_data = data[data_start:end]\n    \n    # For now, let's just visualize the compressed data structure\n    print(f\"\\nFirst 100 bytes of compressed data:\")\n    for i in range(0, min(100, len(compressed_data)), 20):\n        chunk = compressed_data[i:i+20]\n        print(f\"  {i:3d}: {chunk.hex()}\")\n    \n    return compressed_data\n\ndef main():\n    with open(ALFRED7_PATH, 'rb') as f:\n        data = f.read()\n    \n    # Candidate animation\n    buda_offset = 0x1AF3E6\n    \n    print(f\"Analyzing animation at BUDA 0x{buda_offset:06X}\")\n    print(\"=\"*60)\n    \n    # Try different dimension combinations\n    candidates = [\n        (71, 100, 3),   # Brick throw estimate\n        (71, 94, 3),    # From earlier analysis\n        (47, 71, 6),    # Alternative\n        (71, 102, 3),   # Like FIGHT height\n    ]\n    \n    compressed_data = extract_animation(data, buda_offset, 71, 100, 3)\n    \n    # Find BUDA markers around this one\n    print(\"\\n\" + \"=\"*60)\n    print(\"Nearby BUDA markers:\")\n    for i in range(max(0, buda_offset - 50000), min(len(data), buda_offset + 50000)):\n        if data[i:i+4] == b'BUDA':\n            print(f\"  0x{i:06X}\")\n    \n    # Check if this matches FIGHT animation structure\n    print(\"\\n\" + \"=\"*60)\n    print(\"Comparing to FIGHT animation:\")\n    fight_buda = 0x2207F6\n    fight_data = data[fight_buda+4:fight_buda+4+100]\n    print(f\"FIGHT data: {fight_data[:40].hex()}\")\n    print(f\"This data:  {compressed_data[:40].hex()}\")\n\nif __name__ == '__main__':\n    os.makedirs(\"output_throw_anim\", exist_ok=True)\n    main()\n",
  "toolCallResult": null
}
```

```json
  "textEditContent": "#!/usr/bin/env python3\n\"\"\"Calculate file-to-memory mapping.\"\"\"\n\n# mem 0x255CE -&gt; file 0x297CE\n# The conversion: file = mem + 0x4200\n\n# Check play_fight_animation at mem 0x26420\nmem = 0x26420\nfile_expected = mem + 0x4200\nprint(f\"play_fight_animation: mem 0x{mem:05X} -&gt; file 0x{file_expected:05X}\")\n\n# Check MOV EAX, 0x1AF3EA at mem 0x255CE\nmem2 = 0x255CE\nfile_expected2 = mem2 + 0x4200\nprint(f\"MOV EAX, 0x1AF3EA: mem 0x{mem2:05X} -&gt; file 0x{file_expected2:05X}\")\n\n# Verify the instruction at file 0x297CE\nwith open('files/JUEGO.EXE', 'rb') as f:\n    f.seek(0x297CE)\n    data = f.read(5)\n    print(f\"Bytes at file 0x297CE: {data.hex()} (expecting B8EAF31A00)\")\n    \n# So the formula is: file_offset = mem_offset + 0x4200\n# Or: mem_offset = file_offset - 0x4200\n# For Object 1 (loaded at 0x10000), file starts at 0x14200\n# So: mem = file - 0x14200 + 0x10000 = file - 0x4200 ✓\n",

}
```

```json
{
  "invocationMessage": "Creating [](file:///Users/gabriel/Desktop/source/alfredtools/analyze_brick_code.py)",
  "pastTenseMessage": "Created [](file:///Users/gabriel/Desktop/source/alfredtools/analyze_brick_code.py)",
  "isConfirmed": {

  "content": "",
  "textEditContent": "#!/usr/bin/env python3\n\"\"\"Analyze the brick throw animation parameters from the executable.\"\"\"\n\n# From hex dump at 0x255B0-0x255D5:\n# 52           = PUSH EDX\n# 6A 00        = PUSH 0x00\n# 6A 00        = PUSH 0x00  \n# 6A 01        = PUSH 0x01 (compressed flag?)\n# 6A 02        = PUSH 0x02\n# 6A 09        = PUSH 0x09 (wait... this is 9, not 3 frames)\n# 6A 48        = PUSH 0x48 = 72 (width!)\n# 6A 21        = PUSH 0x21 = 33 (not 99...)\n\n# Wait, looking again at 0x255C0:\n# B9 38 00 00 00 = MOV ECX, 0x38 (56)\n# BB 34 01 00 00 = MOV EBX, 0x134 (308) \n# BA EA 0E 00 00 = MOV EDX, 0x0EEA (3818 = compressed size!)\n# B8 EA F3 1A 00 = MOV EAX, 0x1AF3EA (animation offset!)\n# EB C6          = JMP -58\n\n# So the parameters for brick throw are:\n# - EAX = 0x1AF3EA (animation offset in ALFRED.7)\n# - EDX = 0x0EEA = 3818 (compressed data size)\n# - EBX = 0x134 = 308 (maybe width * 4 or something?)\n# - ECX = 0x38 = 56\n\n# But wait, the code at 0x255B0 has:\n# 6A 09 6A 48 6A 21 = PUSH 9, PUSH 72, PUSH 33\n# That could be: frames=9, width=72, height=33 but that doesn't match 72x99\n\n# Let me re-examine. Maybe I'm reading the bytes wrong\nwith open(\"files/JUEGO.EXE\", \"rb\") as f:\n    f.seek(0x297A0)  # mem 0x255A0\n    data = f.read(80)\n    \n    print(\"Code at mem 0x255A0:\")\n    i = 0\n    while i &lt; len(data):\n        addr = 0x255A0 + i\n        b = data[i]\n        \n        # Simple x86 disassembly\n        if b == 0x68:  # PUSH imm32\n            imm = int.from_bytes(data[i+1:i+5], 'little')\n            print(f\"  0x{addr:05X}: PUSH 0x{imm:08X}\")\n            i += 5\n        elif b == 0x6A:  # PUSH imm8\n            imm = data[i+1]\n            print(f\"  0x{addr:05X}: PUSH 0x{imm:02X} ({imm})\")\n            i += 2\n        elif b == 0xB8:  # MOV EAX, imm32\n            imm = int.from_bytes(data[i+1:i+5], 'little')\n            print(f\"  0x{addr:05X}: MOV EAX, 0x{imm:08X}\")\n            i += 5\n        elif b == 0xB9:  # MOV ECX, imm32\n            imm = int.from_bytes(data[i+1:i+5], 'little')\n            print(f\"  0x{addr:05X}: MOV ECX, 0x{imm:08X}\")\n            i += 5\n        elif b == 0xBA:  # MOV EDX, imm32\n            imm = int.from_bytes(data[i+1:i+5], 'little')\n            print(f\"  0x{addr:05X}: MOV EDX, 0x{imm:08X}\")\n            i += 5\n        elif b == 0xBB:  # MOV EBX, imm32\n            imm = int.from_bytes(data[i+1:i+5], 'little')\n            print(f\"  0x{addr:05X}: MOV EBX, 0x{imm:08X}\")\n            i += 5\n        elif b == 0xE8:  # CALL rel32\n            rel = int.from_bytes(data[i+1:i+5], 'little', signed=True)\n            target = addr + 5 + rel\n            print(f\"  0x{addr:05X}: CALL 0x{target:05X}\")\n            i += 5\n        elif b == 0xEB:  # JMP rel8\n            rel = data[i+1]\n            if rel &gt;= 128:\n                rel = rel - 256\n            target = addr + 2 + rel\n            print(f\"  0x{addr:05X}: JMP 0x{target:05X}\")\n            i += 2\n        elif b == 0xC3:  # RET\n            print(f\"  0x{addr:05X}: RET\")\n            i += 1\n        elif b in [0x50, 0x51, 0x52, 0x53]:  # PUSH EAX/ECX/EDX/EBX\n            regs = {0x50: 'EAX', 0x51: 'ECX', 0x52: 'EDX', 0x53: 'EBX'}\n            print(f\"  0x{addr:05X}: PUSH {regs[b]}\")\n            i += 1\n        elif b in [0x58, 0x59, 0x5A, 0x5B]:  # POP EAX/ECX/EDX/EBX\n            regs = {0x58: 'EAX', 0x59: 'ECX', 0x5A: 'EDX', 0x5B: 'EBX'}\n            print(f\"  0x{addr:05X}: POP {regs[b]}\")\n            i += 1\n        elif b == 0x31:  # XOR r32, r32\n            print(f\"  0x{addr:05X}: XOR ...\")\n            i += 2\n        elif b == 0xA0:  # MOV AL, [imm32]\n            imm = int.from_bytes(data[i+1:i+5], 'little')\n            print(f\"  0x{addr:05X}: MOV AL, [0x{imm:08X}]\")\n            i += 5\n        else:\n            print(f\"  0x{addr:05X}: ?? 0x{b:02X}\")\n            i += 1\n        \n        if addr &gt;= 0x255E0:\n            break\n\nprint(\"\\n\" + \"=\"*60)\nprint(\"Summary:\")\nprint(\"=\"*60)\nprint(\"Brick throw animation appears at multiple code locations\")\nprint(\"One block loads: EAX=0x1AF3EA, EDX=0x0EEA (3818 bytes compressed)\")\n",
```

```json
  "content": "",
  "textEditContent": "#!/usr/bin/env python3\n\"\"\"Extract brick throw as 9 frames of 72x33.\"\"\"\n\nimport os\n\ndef decompress_rle(data, max_output=100000):\n    \"\"\"Decompress RLE data until BUDA marker or max output\"\"\"\n    output = []\n    i = 0\n    while i &lt; len(data) - 1 and len(output) &lt; max_output:\n        if i + 3 &lt; len(data) and data[i:i+4] == b'BUDA':\n            return bytes(output), i\n        \n        count = data[i]\n        value = data[i + 1]\n        \n        if count == 0:\n            i += 2\n            continue\n        \n        output.extend([value] * count)\n        i += 2\n    \n    return bytes(output), -1\n\nwith open(\"files/ALFRED.7\", \"rb\") as f:\n    alfred7 = f.read()\n\nos.makedirs(\"output_brick_throw_9frames\", exist_ok=True)\n\ndef save_ppm(data, width, height, filename):\n    with open(filename, \"wb\") as f:\n        f.write(f\"P5\\n{width} {height}\\n255\\n\".encode())\n        f.write(data[:width*height])\n\n# Parameters from code: 9 frames, width=72, height=33\nanim_offset = 0x1AF3EA\nwidth = 72\nheight = 33\nframes = 9\n\nprint(f\"Extracting animation at 0x{anim_offset:06X}\")\nprint(f\"Dimensions: {width}x{height}, {frames} frames\")\nprint(\"=\" * 60)\n\nchunk = alfred7[anim_offset:anim_offset + 30000]\ndecompressed, buda_pos = decompress_rle(chunk)\n\nprint(f\"Decompressed size: {len(decompressed)} bytes\")\nprint(f\"Expected size: {width * height * frames} bytes\")\nprint(f\"BUDA at compressed offset: +0x{buda_pos:04X}\")\n\nframe_size = width * height\n\nfor frame in range(frames):\n    frame_start = frame * frame_size\n    frame_data = decompressed[frame_start:frame_start + frame_size]\n    \n    filename = f\"output_brick_throw_9frames/frame_{frame}.ppm\"\n    save_ppm(frame_data, width, height, filename)\n    \n    # Stats\n    unique = len(set(frame_data))\n    trans = frame_data.count(0xFF)\n    non_trans = frame_size - trans\n    \n    print(f\"Frame {frame}: {non_trans} non-transparent pixels, {unique} colors\")\n\nprint(\"\\nDone! Check output_brick_throw_9frames/ for frames.\")\n",
  "toolCallResult": null
}
```
